newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria seeks compensation for embargo.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria seeks compensation for embargo.

text.p: Bulgaria said on Tuesday it would seek some compensation through the United Nations for the losses it suffered due to the four-year international embargo against neighbouring rump Yugoslavia.

"Bulgaria, which strictly implemented the embargo, will submit to the 51st U.N. session a draft resolution aimed at offsetting losses sustained during the war in ex-Yugoslavia," Deputy Foreign Minister Konstantin Glavanakov told reporters.

Bulgaria could be compensated through participation in post-war reconstruction projects in ex-Yugoslavia, funded by international organisations, or by taking part in tripartite trade operations, he said.

Glavanakov said estimating the exact losses suffered by Bulgaria was very difficult but added the government's sanctions committee put the figure at between seven billion dollars and nine billion dollars.
"We hope other countries also hurt by the embargo, like Ukraine, join our draft resolution," Glavanakov said, adding that most European Union countries had pledged their support for the proposal.

Bulgaria, which shares a 250-mile (400 km) border with ex-Yugoslavia and whose road and and rail links to Europe pass through Serbia, was practically cut off from European markets by the trade embargo during the conflict.
The U.N. Security Council suspended sanctions against Belgrade in November 1995 at the time of the Dayton peace accord.
